name: Eagle
story: Eagle was Apollo 11's lunar module. On July 20, 1969, it carried Neil Armstrong and Edwin 'Buzz' Aldrin from lunar orbit to the Sea of Tranquility and became the vehicle from which humans first stepped onto another world. After the astronauts launched the ascent stage to return to lunar orbit, the descent stage remained at Tranquility Base.

timeline.title: Launch
timeline.text: Apollo 11 launches from Launch Complex 39A aboard Saturn V AS-506.

timeline.title: Lunar orbit
timeline.text: Apollo 11 enters lunar orbit. Armstrong and Aldrin prepare Eagle for descent.

timeline.title: Eagle lands
timeline.text: The lunar module touches down in the Sea of Tranquility. Armstrong reports that the Eagle has landed.

timeline.title: The first footsteps
timeline.text: Armstrong and Aldrin work on the surface, deploy experiments, photograph the site and collect lunar samples.

timeline.title: Ascent
timeline.text: The ascent stage lifts off using the descent stage as its launch platform and later rendezvous with Columbia.

timeline.title: The descent stage stays
timeline.text: The lower stage remains at Tranquility Base as a physical record of the first crewed lunar landing.
